newsitem.title: CANADA: Talisman will not up Wascana bid.
newsitem.headline: Talisman will not up Wascana bid.

text.p: Talisman Energy Inc said on Wednesday it would not increase its C$18.50 a share offer for Wascana Energy Inc after Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd last month came in with a C$20.50 a share bid.
"Our first priority is creating value for Talisman shareholders," Jim Buckee, chief executive of Talisman said in a statement.

"At Talisman's offer price and structure it would have been a good deal -- the overlap in assets, combined with Talisman's operating capabilities would make sense. However, the new price implies paying for all the unrisked upside and more. We can do better things with this amount of money."
Talisman said its offer of C$18.50 a share recognized some of the value it felt could be generated from the Wascana assets.
"Talisman is unable to justify a competing offer. Even the reserves recognized by Wascana's external consultant do not support a higher bid," the company said.

It said the decision was due partly to Wascana's lack of tax pools, the significant heavy oil component in its production and reserves, and future development costs associated with many of its "proven" reserves.

Talisman added that had these concerns not been an issue, the increased price paired with an increasing need to provide cash to satisfy Wascana's changed shareholder base would have required it to raise its debt beyond prudent levels.
"Although Wascana represents a logical fit with our existing assets and technical skills, our decision clearly demonstrates that we don't believe the value is there," Buckee said.
